title: Encrypt every EBS volume
statement: All EBS volumes are encrypted at rest, including the root volumes of EC2 instances and the volumes that launch templates create.

title: EC2 instances use IMDSv2 only
statement: The instance metadata service requires session tokens on every EC2 instance and launch template. IMDSv1 stays disabled.

title: Databases are never reachable from the internet
statement: No RDS instance is publicly accessible. Services reach their database only from inside the VPC.

title: RDS data is encrypted at rest
statement: Every RDS instance and Aurora cluster stores its data encrypted. An unencrypted database is not created.

title: S3 buckets encrypt with our own KMS keys
statement: Bucket encryption uses a customer-managed KMS key that the security team controls, not the AWS-managed S3 key.

title: No public S3 ACLs
statement: No bucket ACL grants public-read, public-read-write or authenticated-read. Access goes through IAM policies.

title: Every S3 bucket blocks public access
statement: Each bucket has a public access block with all four settings turned on, so a later policy cannot make it public.

title: No SSH from the internet
statement: Security groups never allow port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Engineers reach hosts through Session Manager.

title: AKS API servers are private
statement: Every AKS cluster runs with a private API server endpoint. The control plane is not exposed on a public address.

title: Key vaults cannot be purged
statement: Purge protection is on for every Azure key vault, so a deleted vault and its keys can always be recovered.

title: Storage accounts need TLS 1.2
statement: Azure storage accounts reject clients that negotiate a TLS version older than 1.2.

title: PostgreSQL is our only datastore
statement: New databases are PostgreSQL. We do not add MySQL, SQL Server, DynamoDB, Cosmos DB or a Redis cache as a datastore.

title: Outbound HTTP in Go has a timeout
statement: Every http.Client in our Go services sets a Timeout. http.DefaultClient is not used for outbound calls.

title: Go SQL queries use placeholders
statement: Go code passes values to SQL as placeholders. No query is built with fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation.

title: Go services log with slog
statement: Go code logs through log/slog with structured attributes. The standard log package is not used for application logs.

title: No System.out in Java services
statement: Java services log through SLF4J. System.out.println and System.err.println are not used for logging.

title: No eval in the frontend
statement: JavaScript and TypeScript code never calls eval or new Function on a string.

title: No innerHTML in web code
statement: Web code sets text through textContent or the framework's bindings. Nothing assigns to innerHTML.

title: No pickle in Python services
statement: Python services do not deserialize data with pickle. Messages and caches use JSON.

title: Python HTTP calls time out
statement: Every call made with the requests library passes an explicit timeout, so a slow dependency cannot hang a worker.

title: S3 buckets keep object versions
statement: Versioning is enabled on every S3 bucket that holds customer data, so an overwritten object can be restored.

title: Go services log with zap
statement: Go code logs through go.uber.org/zap with structured fields, using the shared logger from the platform module.

title: No SSH from the internet on GCP
statement: google_compute_firewall rules never allow port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0. Engineers connect through Identity-Aware Proxy.

title: Two reviewers for payments code
statement: Every change to the payments service needs approval from two engineers of the payments team before it merges.

title: Pages are acknowledged within fifteen minutes
statement: The on-call engineer acknowledges a page within fifteen minutes and posts a first update in the incident channel.

title: DynamoDB tables can be restored to a point in time
statement: Point-in-time recovery is enabled on every DynamoDB table that the order service owns.

title: Rust crates forbid unsafe code
statement: Every Rust crate in the monorepo declares forbid(unsafe_code). FFI lives in one audited crate.

title: Cloud Storage buckets use uniform access
statement: Google Cloud Storage buckets enable uniform bucket-level access, so object ACLs are never used.

title: Frontend builds use Vite
